title: Advanced Silent Letters (bt, ps-, pn-, sc-)
objectives: Suppress initial silent P in Greek words (ps-, pn-)
Suppress internal silent B in Latinate words (-bt)
Recognize SC soft sound /s/ before E/I

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Advanced Silent Letters (bt, ps-, pn-, sc-). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces /p/ in "pneumonia".
💡 Solution: Explain Greek initial cluster rule: initial P is silent before N and S.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Advanced Silent Letters (bt, ps-, pn-, sc-)
1. Definition: Etymological silent letters in Latinate and Greek loanwords in formal and scientific English.
2. Rule: 1. Initial PS- = /s/ (psychology, psalm). 2. Initial PN- = /n/ (pneumonia, pneumatic). 3. -BT = /t/ (doubt, debt, subtle). 4. SC- before E, I, Y = /s/ (science, scene, muscle).
3. Why? Greek initial clusters ps-/pn- were imprononçable at word start in English; Latin -bt- b was silent in French loanwords.
4. How to recognize? Formal Greek/Latin prefixes ps-, pn-, sc- and root -bt-.
5. Common examples: psychology /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/, psalm /sɑːm/, pneumonia /njuːˈmoʊniə/, doubt /daʊt/, debt /dɛt/, subtle /ˈsʌtəl/, science /ˈsaɪəns/, scene /siːn/
6. Counter-examples: SC before A, O, U = /sk/ hard sound (scale, scope, sculpture).
7. Exceptions: sceptic /ˈskɛptɪk/ (UK spelling with hard /sk/).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing the P in "psychology" (*p-sychology) or B in "debt" (*deb-t).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Initial P before S/N is SILENT! Silent B in doubt & debt!
10. Key vocabulary: silent consonant, Greek loanword, Latin borrowing, initial cluster, formal register
11. Frequency: ★★★☆☆ (Moderate)
12. CEFR Level: 🔵 B2
13. Associated Visual: 👻 Ghost icon over P in ps/pn and B in bt.
14. Key Takeaway: PS=S, PN=N, BT=T! Never pronounce the silent initial P or b in debt/doubt!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: Do you pronounce the P at the start of "psychology"? (No, ps- = /s/)
CCQ 2: Do you pronounce the B in "debt" and "doubt"? (No, -bt = /t/)
CCQ 3: How is SC pronounced before E in "science"? (/s/ sound)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.
